instruments.title: Add BankG, the Swiss Banking Act (Bankengesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Banken und Sparkassen (Bankengesetz, BankG), SR 952.0, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Oktober 2026, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 56: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. März 1935" (footnote: BRB vom 26. Febr. 1935)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über die Banken und Sparkassen (Bankengesetz, BankG)
titles.en: Banking Act (Federal Act on Banks and Savings Banks)

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 8. November 1934 über die Banken und Sparkassen (Bankengesetz, BankG), SR 952.0

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the organisation, capital and proper-conduct conditions of the banking licence
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 3 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Keep the organisation, capital and proper-conduct conditions of the banking licence

summaries.en: A bank is licensed only if its articles and regulations define its business precisely and provide an organisation fitting that business, with separate bodies for management and for direction, supervision and control where its purpose or size requires, and if it shows the fully paid-up minimum capital the Federal Council sets. The persons entrusted with its administration and management must be of good repute and assure proper business conduct, managers must live where they can actually run the business, and holders of 10 per cent or more of capital or votes must ensure their influence does not harm prudent and sound business.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Notify FINMA of changes to the articles, of qualified shareholders and before setting up abroad
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 3 Abs. 3, 6 und 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Notify FINMA of changes to the articles, of qualified shareholders and before setting up abroad

summaries.en: A bank must file its articles, partnership agreements and regulations with FINMA and notify every later change that concerns its purpose, business scope, capital or internal organisation; such a change may not be entered in the commercial register before FINMA has approved it. It must report the persons who acquire or sell a qualified participation, or cross the 20, 33 or 50 per cent thresholds, as soon as it learns of them and at least once a year. A bank organised under Swiss law must notify FINMA before it sets up a subsidiary, branch, agency or representative office abroad.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold adequate own funds and liquidity and cap holdings outside the financial sector
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 4 Abs. 1 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Hold adequate own funds and liquidity and cap holdings outside the financial sector

summaries.en: A bank must have adequate own funds and liquidity, on its own and on a consolidated basis; the Federal Council sets the minimum requirements. A qualified participation in a company outside the financial and insurance sector may not exceed 15 per cent of the bank's own funds, and all such participations together may not exceed 60 per cent, subject to the exceptions the Federal Council allows.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep loans to a single client and holdings in a single company in proportion to own funds
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 4bis Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Keep loans to a single client and holdings in a single company in proportion to own funds

summaries.en: A bank's lending to any one client and its participations in any one company must stand in an appropriate ratio to its own funds. The implementing ordinance sets that ratio.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Grant loans to members of the bank's bodies and major shareholders only on recognised banking principles
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 4ter Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Grant loans to members of the bank's bodies and major shareholders only on recognised banking principles

summaries.en: A bank may grant loans to members of its governing bodies, to its major shareholders and to persons and companies close to them only in line with the generally recognised principles of the banking trade.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Draw up an annual report and half-yearly interim accounts and publish the annual report
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 6 und 6a, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Draw up an annual report and half-yearly interim accounts and publish the annual report

summaries.en: A bank must draw up for each financial year an annual report made up of the annual accounts, the management report and the consolidated accounts, and interim accounts at least every half year, under the accounting rules of the Code of Obligations, this act and their implementing provisions. The annual report must be made available to the public, and interim accounts where the implementing provisions require it. Private bankers who do not publicly solicit deposits are exempt from publication.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Appoint a licensed audit firm for the regulatory audit and have the accounts audited
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 18, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Appoint a licensed audit firm for the regulatory audit and have the accounts audited

summaries.en: Banks, financial groups and financial conglomerates must mandate an audit firm licensed by the Federal Audit Oversight Authority to carry out the audit under Article 24 of the Financial Market Supervision Act. They must also have their annual accounts, and consolidated accounts where they have them, audited by a state-supervised audit firm under the ordinary audit rules of the Code of Obligations.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Meet the special requirements for systemically important banks and prove a workable emergency plan
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 9 Abs. 2 und Art. 10 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Meet the special requirements for systemically important banks and prove a workable emergency plan

summaries.en: A systemically important bank must hold own funds with a higher loss-absorbing capacity and liquidity that absorbs shocks better than other banks, spread its risks so that counterparty and concentration risks are limited, and have an emergency plan for its structure, infrastructure, management and control and its intra-group liquidity and capital flows that can be put into effect at once. It must prove that it meets the emergency planning requirement and can continue its systemically important functions if insolvency threatens; if it does not, FINMA orders the necessary measures.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold Swiss assets worth 125 per cent of privileged deposits at all times
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 37a Abs. 1 und 6, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Hold Swiss assets worth 125 per cent of privileged deposits at all times

summaries.en: A bank must at all times hold domestically covered claims or other assets located in Switzerland worth 125 per cent of its privileged deposits, which are deposits in the depositor's name up to 100,000 francs per creditor. FINMA may raise the share and may grant exceptions in justified cases, in particular to institutions whose business structure gives equivalent cover.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Join the banks' deposit insurance scheme and prepare for a payout
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 37h Abs. 1, 3 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Join the banks' deposit insurance scheme and prepare for a payout

summaries.en: Before taking privileged deposits at Swiss offices a bank must join the banks' self-regulation that secures those deposits, which FINMA approves. The self-regulation obliges the banks to contributions of 1.6 per cent of all secured deposits and at least 6 billion francs in total, and each bank to keep half of its contribution obligation permanently deposited in high-quality liquid securities or Swiss francs with a safe custodian or lent in cash to the scheme. It also obliges each bank to prepare in the ordinary course of business the infrastructure, standard processes, depositor list and summary of other privileged deposits needed for a payout plan and payment; a transitional provision gives that last requirement five years from the entry into force of the amendment of 17 December 2021.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Liquidate dormant assets after 50 years following publication
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BankG (SR 952.0), Art. 37m Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Liquidate dormant assets after 50 years following publication

summaries.en: A bank liquidates dormant assets after 50 years if the entitled person does not come forward after prior publication; assets of no more than 500 francs may be liquidated without publication. The entitled person's claim lapses on liquidation and the proceeds go to the Confederation.

instruments.title: Add FINIG, the Swiss Financial Institutions Act (Finanzinstitutsgesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Finanzinstitute (Finanzinstitutsgesetz, FINIG), SR 954.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Oktober 2026, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 75: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. Januar 2020" (footnote: V vom 6. Nov. 2019, AS 2019 4631)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über die Finanzinstitute (Finanzinstitutsgesetz, FINIG)
titles.en: Financial Institutions Act

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 15. Juni 2018 über die Finanzinstitute (Finanzinstitutsgesetz, FINIG), SR 954.1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report changes to the facts behind the licence and get approval for material ones
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 8, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Report changes to the facts behind the licence and get approval for material ones

summaries.en: A financial institution must report to FINMA every change in the facts on which its licence rests. Where a change is of material importance, it must obtain FINMA's approval before it continues the activity.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set governance rules and identify, measure, steer and monitor risks
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 9 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Set governance rules and identify, measure, steer and monitor risks

summaries.en: A financial institution must lay down appropriate rules of corporate governance and be organised so that it can meet its statutory duties. It identifies, measures, steers and monitors its risks, legal and reputational risks included, and ensures effective internal controls.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Run the institution from Switzerland
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 10, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Run the institution from Switzerland

summaries.en: A financial institution must actually be managed from Switzerland; general instructions and decisions of group supervision are excepted where the institution belongs to a financial group under appropriate consolidated supervision by foreign authorities. The persons entrusted with its management must live in a place from which they can actually carry out the management.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assure proper business conduct and report holders of qualified participations
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 11 Abs. 1, 2, 6 und 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Assure proper business conduct and report holders of qualified participations

summaries.en: A financial institution and the persons entrusted with its administration and management must assure proper business conduct, and those persons must be of good repute and have the professional qualifications their function needs. The institution reports to FINMA, as soon as it learns of them, the persons who acquire or sell a qualified participation of 10 per cent or more or cross the 20, 33 or 50 per cent thresholds. Portfolio managers and trustees are exempt from that reporting.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Delegate tasks only to capable and licensed third parties and supervise them
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 14 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Delegate tasks only to capable and licensed third parties and supervise them

summaries.en: A financial institution may delegate a task only to third parties that have the skills, knowledge and experience the activity needs and hold the licences it requires. It must instruct and supervise them carefully.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold adequate own funds and liquidity and spread risks as a securities firm
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 46 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Hold adequate own funds and liquidity and spread risks as a securities firm

summaries.en: A securities firm must have adequate own funds and liquidity, on its own and on a consolidated basis, and must spread its risks appropriately. The Federal Council sets the amounts and the risk-spreading requirements, and FINMA may grant relief or order stricter terms in justified cases.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Record every order and transaction as a securities firm
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 50, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Record every order and transaction as a securities firm

summaries.en: A securities firm must record the orders it receives and the transactions it carries out with all the details needed to trace them and to supervise its activity.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File the reports needed for transparent securities trading as a securities firm
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 51 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: File the reports needed for transparent securities trading as a securities firm

summaries.en: A securities firm must file the reports that are needed for the transparency of securities trading. FINMA determines which information is reported to whom and in what form.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have a licensed audit firm audit the institution every year and report on conformity in years without an audit
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINIG (SR 954.1), Art. 63 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Have a licensed audit firm audit the institution every year and report on conformity in years without an audit

summaries.en: Managers of collective assets, fund management companies, securities firms, financial groups and financial conglomerates must mandate an audit firm licensed by the Federal Audit Oversight Authority for a yearly audit under Article 24 of the Financial Market Supervision Act, and have their annual and any consolidated accounts audited by a state-supervised audit firm under the ordinary audit rules of the Code of Obligations. FINMA may allow an audit cycle of several years; in a year without a periodic audit the institution sends FINMA a report on the conformity of its business with the law.

instruments.title: Add FIDLEG, the Swiss Financial Services Act (Finanzdienstleistungsgesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Finanzdienstleistungen (Finanzdienstleistungsgesetz, FIDLEG), SR 950.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Oktober 2026, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 96: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. Januar 2020" (footnote: V vom 6. Nov. 2019 über die abschliessende Inkraftsetzung des Finanzinstitutsgesetzes, AS 2019 4631)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über die Finanzdienstleistungen (Finanzdienstleistungsgesetz, FIDLEG)
titles.en: Financial Services Act

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 15. Juni 2018 über die Finanzdienstleistungen (Finanzdienstleistungsgesetz, FIDLEG), SR 950.1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Assign every client to the retail, professional or institutional segment
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 4 Abs. 1 und 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Assign every client to the retail, professional or institutional segment

summaries.en: A financial service provider must assign each person it serves to one of three segments: retail clients, professional clients or institutional clients. It may do without the segmentation if it treats all clients as retail clients.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Inform clients about the firm, the service, its risks and its costs before the contract
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 8 Abs. 1, 2 und 6, Art. 9 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Inform clients about the firm, the service, its risks and its costs before the contract

summaries.en: Before the contract is concluded or the service provided, a financial service provider must tell its clients its name and address, its field of activity and supervisory status, that mediation before a recognised ombudsman is available, and the general risks of financial instruments. It must also inform them about the service it personally recommends with its risks and costs, its economic ties to third parties in connection with the service, and the market offer it considered when selecting instruments, and must mark advertising as such. The rules do not apply to institutional clients, and professional clients may expressly waive them.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give retail clients the key information document before they subscribe
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 8 Abs. 3 und 4, Art. 9 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Give retail clients the key information document before they subscribe

summaries.en: When it personally recommends a financial instrument for which a key information document has to be drawn up, a financial service provider must give the retail client that document free of charge before subscription or conclusion of the contract. Where advice is given at a distance, the document may be handed over after the transaction if the client consents and the consent is documented. No document is needed where the service is only the execution or transmission of orders, unless one already exists for the instrument.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check appropriateness or suitability before advising or managing assets
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 10 bis 12, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Check appropriateness or suitability before advising or managing assets

summaries.en: A financial service provider that gives investment advice or manages assets must carry out an appropriateness or a suitability check. When it advises on single transactions without regard to the whole portfolio, it must ask about the client's knowledge and experience and check before recommending that the instrument is appropriate. When it advises with regard to the portfolio or manages assets, it must ask about the client's financial situation and investment objectives as well as knowledge and experience.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell clients when no check is made, when an assessment is impossible or when a product is unsuitable
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 13 Abs. 2 und Art. 14, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Tell clients when no check is made, when an assessment is impossible or when a product is unsuitable

summaries.en: For the mere execution or transmission of orders a financial service provider must tell clients beforehand that it carries out no appropriateness or suitability check. Where the information it receives is not enough to assess a financial instrument, it must tell the client before providing the service that it cannot make the assessment, and where it considers an instrument not appropriate or not suitable it must advise the client against it beforehand.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Document services and client information and account for them on request
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 15 und 16, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Document services and client information and account for them on request

summaries.en: A financial service provider must document the services agreed with clients and the information collected about them, the notices and warnings given under Articles 13 and 14, and the services provided; for investment advice it also documents the client's needs and the reasons for each recommendation that leads to a purchase or sale. On request it gives clients a copy of this documentation and accounts for the services agreed and provided, the composition, valuation and development of the portfolio, and the costs. Professional clients may expressly waive these rules, and they do not apply to institutional clients.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Handle client orders fairly and execute them on the best possible terms
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 17 Abs. 1 und Art. 18, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Handle client orders fairly and execute them on the best possible terms

summaries.en: A financial service provider must handle client orders in good faith and treat clients equally, and must ensure that orders are executed with the best possible result in terms of cost, timing and quality. On cost it takes into account the price of the instrument, the costs of execution and any third-party compensation. If it employs staff who execute client orders, it issues instructions on execution that fit their number and its structure.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Prevent conflicts of interest or disclose them to clients
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 25 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Prevent conflicts of interest or disclose them to clients

summaries.en: A financial service provider must take appropriate organisational measures to avoid conflicts of interest that can arise when it provides financial services, or to rule out that clients are disadvantaged by them. Where a disadvantage cannot be ruled out, it must disclose this to the clients.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Accept third-party compensation only after informing the client or pass it on in full
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 26, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Accept third-party compensation only after informing the client or pass it on in full

summaries.en: A financial service provider may accept compensation from third parties in connection with a financial service only if it has expressly informed the clients about it beforehand and they waive it, or if it passes the compensation on to them in full. The information must state the type and amount before the service is provided or the contract concluded, or the calculation parameters and ranges where the amount cannot be known in advance, and the amounts actually received are disclosed on request.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Publish a prospectus before a public offer of securities or an admission to trading
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 35 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Publish a prospectus before a public offer of securities or an admission to trading

summaries.en: Anyone who makes a public offer in Switzerland to acquire securities, or who applies for securities to be admitted to trading on a trading venue within the meaning of the Financial Market Infrastructure Act, must first publish a prospectus. The act lists exemptions by type of offer and type of security in Articles 36 to 38.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Draw up a key information document before offering a financial instrument to retail clients
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 58 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Draw up a key information document before offering a financial instrument to retail clients

summaries.en: Where a financial instrument is offered to retail clients, its producer must first draw up a key information document. None is needed for instruments that retail clients may acquire only under an asset management contract.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Join an ombudsman, take part in its proceedings and tell clients about it
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FIDLEG (SR 950.1), Art. 77 bis 79, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Join an ombudsman, take part in its proceedings and tell clients about it

summaries.en: A financial service provider that does not serve only institutional or professional clients must join an ombudsman by the time it starts its activity. It must take part in mediation proceedings that concern it and answer the ombudsman's summonses and requests on time. It tells clients about the possibility of mediation, with the ombudsman's name and address, when the relationship begins, when it rejects a claim a client has asserted, and at any time on request.

instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Finanzmarktinfrastrukturen und das Marktverhalten im Effekten- und Derivatehandel (Finanzmarktinfrastrukturgesetz, FinfraG), SR 958.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. titles.en: Financial Market Infrastructure Act (Federal Act on Financial Market Infrastructures and Market Conduct in Securities and Derivatives Trading)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Record orders and transactions as a participant in a trading venue
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 38, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Record orders and transactions as a participant in a trading venue

summaries.en: A participant admitted to a trading venue must record the orders it receives and the transactions it carries out with all the details needed to trace them and to supervise its activity.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File the reports needed for transparent securities trading as a participant in a trading venue
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 39 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: File the reports needed for transparent securities trading as a participant in a trading venue

summaries.en: A participant admitted to a trading venue must file the reports that are needed for the transparency of securities trading. FINMA determines which information is passed on to whom and in what form.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Clear the OTC derivatives FINMA designates through a central counterparty
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 97 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Clear the OTC derivatives FINMA designates through a central counterparty

summaries.en: Counterparties must clear transactions in the derivatives that FINMA designates for clearing, when these are not traded on a trading venue, through a central counterparty that FINMA has licensed or recognised. The duty does not apply to transactions with small counterparties or between small counterparties.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report derivatives transactions to a trade repository by the next working day
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 104 und Art. 105 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Report derivatives transactions to a trade repository by the next working day

summaries.en: Derivatives transactions must be reported to a trade repository that FINMA has licensed or recognised, at the latest on the working day after the transaction is concluded, amended or ended. Between a financial and a non-financial counterparty the financial counterparty reports; between two financial counterparties the one that is not small reports, or the seller where both are small or both are not; the Swiss counterparty reports where a foreign counterparty does not, and the central counterparty reports a centrally cleared transaction. Each report gives at least the counterparties' identity, the type, maturity, notional value, price, settlement date and currency.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the records of derivatives transactions under the accounting retention rules
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 106, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Keep the records of derivatives transactions under the accounting retention rules

summaries.en: Counterparties must keep the records of their derivatives transactions in accordance with Article 958f of the Code of Obligations.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Confirm, reconcile and compress OTC derivatives that are not centrally cleared
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 107 und 108, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Confirm, reconcile and compress OTC derivatives that are not centrally cleared

summaries.en: For OTC derivatives that do not have to be centrally cleared, counterparties must record, monitor and mitigate operational and counterparty risk. They must confirm the terms of each transaction in good time, have procedures to reconcile portfolios, except for a small non-financial counterparty, and to detect and settle disputes early, and carry out a portfolio compression at least twice a year where this is suited to reducing counterparty risk and they have 500 or more uncleared OTC transactions outstanding. The duties do not apply to currency swaps and forwards settled payment versus payment or to transactions cleared voluntarily.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Value outstanding derivatives every day and exchange collateral
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 109 und 110, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Value outstanding derivatives every day and exchange collateral

summaries.en: Counterparties must value their outstanding uncleared OTC derivatives every day at current prices, or by an appropriate and recognised valuation model where market conditions do not allow marking to market; this does not apply to transactions with small counterparties. Counterparties other than small non-financial ones must exchange appropriate collateral and be able to keep it appropriately separate from their own assets.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Trade the derivatives FINMA designates on a trading venue or an organised trading facility
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 112, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Trade the derivatives FINMA designates on a trading venue or an organised trading facility

summaries.en: Counterparties must trade the derivatives that FINMA designates for this duty on a trading venue, or through the operator of an organised trading facility, that FINMA has licensed or recognised. The duty does not apply to transactions with small counterparties or between small counterparties.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Disclose holdings in listed companies that reach, exceed or fall below the voting-right thresholds
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 120 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Disclose holdings in listed companies that reach, exceed or fall below the voting-right thresholds

summaries.en: Anyone who, directly, indirectly or acting in concert with others, acquires or sells shares or rights to acquire or sell shares in a company based in Switzerland whose equity securities are listed there, or in a foreign company whose equity securities have their main listing there, and thereby reaches, exceeds or falls below 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 33⅓, 50 or 66⅔ per cent of the voting rights, must notify the company and the stock exchanges where the securities are listed. The duty also binds anyone who can exercise the voting rights at their own discretion. Financial intermediaries that acquire or sell for the account of third parties are not subject to it.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not use, pass on or recommend on the basis of inside information
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 142 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Do not use, pass on or recommend on the basis of inside information

summaries.en: It is unlawful for anyone who knows or must know that information is inside information, or that a recommendation rests on it, to use it to acquire or sell securities admitted to trading on a trading venue or DLT trading facility based in Switzerland or to use derivatives of them, to disclose it to another person, or to use it to recommend such a transaction to another person.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not spread false signals or place misleading orders in securities
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FinfraG (SR 958.1), Art. 143 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Februar 2024

titles.en: Do not spread false signals or place misleading orders in securities

summaries.en: It is unlawful to spread information publicly, or to carry out transactions or place buy or sell orders, when the person knows or must know that they give false or misleading signals for the supply, demand or price of securities admitted to trading on a trading venue or DLT trading facility based in Switzerland.

instruments.title: Add KAG, the Swiss Collective Investment Schemes Act (Kollektivanlagengesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die kollektiven Kapitalanlagen (Kollektivanlagengesetz, KAG), SR 951.31, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Oktober 2026, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 159: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. Januar 2007" (footnote: BRB vom 22. Nov. 2006)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über die kollektiven Kapitalanlagen (Kollektivanlagengesetz, KAG)
titles.en: Collective Investment Schemes Act

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 23. Juni 2006 über die kollektiven Kapitalanlagen (Kollektivanlagengesetz, KAG), SR 951.31

obligations.title: Add the duty: Obtain FINMA's licence and its approval of the fund documents
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 13 Abs. 1, 2 und 2bis, Art. 15 Abs. 1 und 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Obtain FINMA's licence and its approval of the fund documents

summaries.en: Anyone who forms, operates or keeps a collective investment scheme needs a licence from FINMA; investment companies with variable or fixed capital, limited partnerships for collective investment, custodian banks and representatives of foreign schemes must apply for one. The fund contract, the articles and investment regulations of an investment company, the partnership agreement and the corresponding documents of foreign schemes offered to non-qualified investors need FINMA's approval. A limited qualified investor fund set up as an investment company with variable capital or a limited partnership needs no licence, and the documents of such a fund need no approval.

payload.refLabel: Art. 13 Abs. 1, 2 und 2bis, Art. 15 Abs. 1 und 3

obligations.title: Add the duty: Get FINMA's approval before continuing when the licensed circumstances change
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 16, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Get FINMA's approval before continuing when the licensed circumstances change

summaries.en: If the circumstances on which a licence or an approval rests change, FINMA's licence or approval must be obtained before the activity is continued.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Act loyally, carefully and transparently towards fund investors
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 20 Abs. 1 und 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Act loyally, carefully and transparently towards fund investors

summaries.en: Persons who manage, keep or represent collective investment schemes, and their agents, must act independently and solely in the investors' interest, take the organisational measures that proper business conduct requires, and account for the schemes they manage, keep or represent. They must inform investors of all fees and costs charged to them directly or indirectly and of compensation received from third parties, such as commissions and rebates, and take all measures needed to meet these duties across their whole business.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Follow the fund's stated investment policy and take only the remuneration its documents provide
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 21, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Follow the fund's stated investment policy and take only the remuneration its documents provide

summaries.en: Persons who manage, keep or represent collective investment schemes, and their agents, must follow an investment policy that always matches the investment character laid down in the scheme's documents. On buying and selling assets they may take for themselves or third parties only the remuneration those documents provide, must credit third-party compensation to the scheme, and may take over investments for their own account or transfer investments from their own holdings only at the market price.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the fund's assets and check that the fund obeys the law and its rules as custodian bank
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 72 Abs. 1 und Art. 73 Abs. 1 und 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Keep the fund's assets and check that the fund obeys the law and its rules as custodian bank

summaries.en: The custodian bank must be a bank under the Banking Act with an organisation suited to that role. It keeps the fund's assets and handles the issue and redemption of units and the payments. It ensures that the fund management company or investment company observes the law and the fund regulations, checking that the net asset value and the issue and redemption prices are calculated, investment decisions taken and income used in line with them.

payload.refLabel: Art. 72 Abs. 1 und Art. 73 Abs. 1 und 3

obligations.title: Add the duty: Delegate custody of fund assets only to suitable sub-custodians and tell investors the risks
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 73 Abs. 2 und 2bis, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Delegate custody of fund assets only to suitable sub-custodians and tell investors the risks

summaries.en: The custodian bank may entrust the safekeeping of fund assets to third-party and central custodians in Switzerland or abroad where this serves proper custody, and investors must be told the risks of doing so in the prospectus and the key information document. Financial instruments may be entrusted only to supervised custodians, unless custody is mandatory in a place where that is not possible, in which case investors are informed in the product documentation.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Calculate the net asset value at market value and publish it regularly
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 83 Abs. 1, 2 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Calculate the net asset value at market value and publish it regularly

summaries.en: The net asset value of an open-ended collective investment scheme is calculated at market value at the end of the financial year and for every day on which units are issued or redeemed. The value per unit is the market value of the investments less any liabilities, divided by the number of units in circulation. The fund management company and the investment company with variable capital publish the net asset values at regular intervals.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Publish an annual report within four months and a half-yearly report within two months
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 89, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Publish an annual report within four months and a half-yearly report within two months

summaries.en: For every open-ended collective investment scheme an annual report must be published within four months of the end of the financial year, with the annual accounts, the units issued and redeemed, the inventory at market value, the valuation principles, the purchases and sales, the delegates, matters of particular importance, the performance and the audit firm's short report. A half-yearly report with unaudited accounts must be published within two months of the end of the first half of the year. Both are filed with FINMA at the latest on publication and kept available free of charge to interested persons for ten years.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Have a foreign fund approved by FINMA before offering it to non-qualified investors
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KAG (SR 951.31), Art. 120 Abs. 1, 2 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Have a foreign fund approved by FINMA before offering it to non-qualified investors

summaries.en: A foreign collective investment scheme must be approved by FINMA before it is offered in Switzerland to non-qualified investors, and its representative submits the documents that need approval. Approval requires, among other things, public supervision serving investor protection, rules equivalent to this act, a name that does not mislead, a representative and a paying agent for the units offered in Switzerland, and a cooperation agreement between FINMA and the relevant foreign supervisors. A foreign scheme offered to qualified investors needs no approval but must at all times have a name that does not mislead and a representative and paying agent.

instruments.title: Add BEG, the Swiss Intermediated Securities Act (Bucheffektengesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über Bucheffekten (Bucheffektengesetz, BEG), SR 957.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Oktober 2026, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 36: "Inkrafttreten: 1. Januar 2010; Art. 470 Abs. 2bis des Obligationenrechts (Ziff. 3 des Anhang): 1. Oktober 2009" (footnote: BRB vom 6. Mai 2009)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über Bucheffekten (Bucheffektengesetz, BEG)
titles.en: Federal Intermediated Securities Act

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 3. Oktober 2008 über Bucheffekten (Bucheffektengesetz, BEG), SR 957.1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold intermediated securities that cover all clients' credit balances
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BEG (SR 957.1), Art. 11 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Hold intermediated securities that cover all clients' credit balances

summaries.en: Every custodian must keep available, with itself or with a sub-custodian, intermediated securities whose number and type at least equal the sum of the securities shown as credit balances in its account holders' securities accounts. If the available securities fall short of that sum, the custodian must acquire securities to the extent of the shortfall without delay.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep own holdings and clients' holdings separate, in the books and at sub-custodians
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BEG (SR 957.1), Art. 11a Abs. 1 bis 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Keep own holdings and clients' holdings separate, in the books and at sub-custodians

summaries.en: A custodian must keep its own holdings and third-party holdings separate in its books, and where it holds both with a sub-custodian in Switzerland it must hold them in different securities accounts. For custody abroad the Swiss custodian agrees with the first foreign sub-custodian that it keeps them in different accounts or, where that is not possible under the foreign law or for operational reasons, takes other measures that give the account holder comparable protection. No such measures are needed where the securities can be held only in that state or the account holder has instructed custody there in writing or another text form.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell account holders in advance about sub-custody, its risks and costs and about data transfers
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BEG (SR 957.1), Art. 11a Abs. 6 und Art. 11b Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Tell account holders in advance about sub-custody, its risks and costs and about data transfers

summaries.en: A Swiss custodian that holds third-party holdings with a sub-custodian must give the account holder standardised information beforehand, on paper or electronically: that custody is as a rule with a sub-custodian, that the sub-custodian may be based abroad and custody then falls under foreign law, the general risks of custody abroad, and the costs of custody. It must likewise tell account holders beforehand that data may be passed to sub-custodians and other bodies in the custody chain and that client data may, depending on the foreign law, be forwarded to the authorities of the state concerned.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Dispose of clients' securities only under an authorisation and after transfer to the own account
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BEG (SR 957.1), Art. 12 Abs. 2 und Art. 22, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Dispose of clients' securities only under an authorisation and after transfer to the own account

summaries.en: A custodian may dispose of an account holder's intermediated securities in its own name and for its own account only if the account holder has granted it that right, and only after it has transferred them into its own securities account in exercise of the right. Where the account holder is not a qualified investor, the authorisation must be given in writing and may not be contained in the general terms and conditions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Carry out account holders' instructions and give a statement of holdings on request
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BEG (SR 957.1), Art. 15 Abs. 1 und Art. 16, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Carry out account holders' instructions and give a statement of holdings on request

summaries.en: A custodian must carry out the account holder's instructions to dispose of intermediated securities in accordance with its contract with the account holder. The account holder may at any time require a statement of the intermediated securities credited to the securities account.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Reverse a debit made without a valid instruction
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, BEG (SR 957.1), Art. 27 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Reverse a debit made without a valid instruction

summaries.en: A debit of intermediated securities in a securities account must be reversed if it was made without an instruction, on an instruction that was void, did not come from the account holder or their representative, was revoked in time or was contested for error, deception or duress, or if the credit to the acquirer does not match the instruction or is not made within the usual time. The account holder must prove the defect, and there is no claim where the custodian proves that it did not know of the defect and need not have known despite reasonable measures and procedures. The reversal puts the account holder in the position as if the debit had never happened; qualified investors may agree otherwise.

instruments.title: Add PfG, the Swiss Pfandbrief Act on covered mortgage bonds (Pfandbriefgesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Pfandbriefgesetz (PfG), SR 211.423.4, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Januar 2023, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 52: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. Februar 1931" (footnote: BRB vom 23. Jan. 1931, AS 47 120)

titles.de: Pfandbriefgesetz (PfG)
titles.en: Mortgage Bond Act (Pfandbrief Act)

payload.officialRef: Pfandbriefgesetz vom 25. Juni 1930 (PfG), SR 211.423.4

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep loans from the Pfandbrief institution covered at all times by Swiss mortgage claims
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfG (SR 211.423.4), Art. 19 und 20, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Keep loans from the Pfandbrief institution covered at all times by Swiss mortgage claims

summaries.en: The loans a Pfandbrief central institution grants to its members, with the interest outstanding on them, must be covered at all times by the members' mortgage claims or pledge-secured claims against their own borrowers, which the members keep and administer. The mortgaged properties must lie in Switzerland and the pledges must consist of domestic mortgage claims or Pfandbriefe. If the interest yield of a member's cover is lower than that of its loans, the cover must be increased accordingly.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Enter the cover for Pfandbrief loans in a cover register
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfG (SR 211.423.4), Art. 21 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Enter the cover for Pfandbrief loans in a cover register

summaries.en: A member must enter the cover it holds for the loans it has drawn from the Pfandbrief central institution in a cover register. The Federal Council regulates the details of the entry.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the registered cover apart from other assets and enforce its claims
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfG (SR 211.423.4), Art. 22, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Keep the registered cover apart from other assets and enforce its claims

summaries.en: A member must keep the cover entered in its cover register separate from its other assets. It must assert all claims arising from that cover in its own name, in the interest of its central institution.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Top up missing cover with listed public-sector bonds or cash
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfG (SR 211.423.4), Art. 25 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Top up missing cover with listed public-sector bonds or cash

summaries.en: If the prescribed cover is not fully in place and the shortfall cannot be remedied at once, the cover must be supplemented with exchange-listed bonds of the Confederation, the cantons or the municipalities, or with cash. The bonds may be counted at no more than 95 per cent of their current market price.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Count mortgage claims as cover only up to two thirds of the property's market value
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, PfG (SR 211.423.4), Art. 34, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2023

titles.en: Count mortgage claims as cover only up to two thirds of the property's market value

summaries.en: Taking prior liens and secured interest into account, mortgage claims qualify as cover for Pfandbriefe or loans only up to two thirds of the market value of the property. For land used mainly for agriculture or forestry the limit is five sixths of the yield value where such a valuation exists, and never more than two thirds of the market value.

instruments.title: Add KKG, the Swiss Consumer Credit Act (Konsumkreditgesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über den Konsumkredit (KKG), SR 221.214.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. September 2023, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 42: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. Jan. 2003; Art. 39 und 40: 1. Jan. 2004" (footnote: BRB vom 6. Nov. 2002)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über den Konsumkredit (KKG)
titles.en: Consumer Credit Act

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 23. März 2001 über den Konsumkredit (KKG), SR 221.214.1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Conclude cash credit agreements in writing with the required content and give the consumer a copy
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 9, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Conclude cash credit agreements in writing with the required content and give the consumer a copy

summaries.en: A consumer credit agreement must be concluded in writing and the consumer receives a copy. It must state, among other things, the net amount of the credit, the effective annual interest rate, the conditions under which the rate and costs can change, the repayment arrangements, the consumer's right to a reduction on early repayment, the right of withdrawal and its period, any security required and the attachable part of income on which the creditworthiness check rested. A breach makes the agreement void under Article 15.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Put overdraft and card credit agreements in writing and tell the consumer of every rate or cost change
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 12, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Put overdraft and card credit agreements in writing and tell the consumer of every rate or cost change

summaries.en: An agreement granting credit as an overdraft on a current account or on a credit or customer card account with a credit option must be concluded in writing, with a copy for the consumer, and must state the credit limit, the annual interest and costs and how they can change, how the agreement ends and the elements on which the creditworthiness check rested. During the agreement the consumer must be told without delay of every change in the annual interest or the costs, which may be done by account statement. Where an overdraft is tacitly accepted and lasts longer than three months, the consumer must be told the annual interest, the costs and every change to them.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the interest rate within the maximum the Federal Council sets
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 14, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Keep the interest rate within the maximum the Federal Council sets

summaries.en: The Federal Council sets the highest permissible interest rate for consumer credit, taking into account the refinancing rates the Swiss National Bank determines; as a rule the maximum rate is not to exceed 15 per cent. An agreement that does not keep to it is void under Article 15.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Respect the consumer's right to withdraw within 14 days
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 16 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Respect the consumer's right to withdraw within 14 days

summaries.en: The consumer may withdraw the offer to conclude the agreement or the acceptance in writing within 14 days. The period starts once the consumer has received a copy of the agreement and is met if the withdrawal is handed to the lender or the post on its last day. There is no right of withdrawal for a tacitly accepted overdraft.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check the consumer's creditworthiness before concluding the agreement
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 27a und Art. 28 Abs. 2 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Check the consumer's creditworthiness before concluding the agreement

summaries.en: A commercial lender or crowdlending intermediary must check the consumer's creditworthiness before the agreement is concluded. The consumer is creditworthy if the credit can be repaid without drawing on the part of income that cannot be attached under debt enforcement law, calculated under the subsistence guidelines of the canton of residence and taking into account in every case the rent actually owed, the taxes due under the withholding tax table and the commitments reported to the information office. The assessment must assume repayment within 36 months even where a longer term is agreed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check creditworthiness in summary form before granting a card or overdraft credit limit
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 30, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Check creditworthiness in summary form before granting a card or overdraft credit limit

summaries.en: Before granting a credit limit on a credit or customer card account with a credit option or as an overdraft on a current account, the commercial lender or card company must check the applicant's creditworthiness in summary form, relying on the applicant's statements on income and assets. The limit must reflect the consumer's income and assets and take into account the consumer credits reported to the information office. The check must be repeated when the lender learns that the consumer's economic circumstances have worsened.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report consumer credits, arrears and card balances to the consumer credit information office
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 25 Abs. 1 und Art. 27 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Report consumer credits, arrears and card balances to the consumer credit information office

summaries.en: A commercial lender or crowdlending intermediary must report to the information office for consumer credit each credit it grants or arranges and outstanding instalments that amount to at least 10 per cent of the net amount of the credit or of the cash price. Where a consumer has used the credit option of a credit or customer card account three times in a row, the outstanding amount must be reported unless it is below 3,000 francs.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not advertise consumer credit aggressively
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, KKG (SR 221.214.1), Art. 36a Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Do not advertise consumer credit aggressively

summaries.en: Consumer credit may not be advertised in an aggressive manner. Commercial lenders define in a private-law agreement, in an appropriate way, which advertising counts as aggressive; the Federal Council regulates it if no adequate agreement is reached within a reasonable time.

instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Schweizerische Nationalbank (Nationalbankgesetz, NBG), SR 951.11, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. titles.en: National Bank Act (Federal Act on the Swiss National Bank)

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 3. Oktober 2003 über die Schweizerische Nationalbank (Nationalbankgesetz, NBG), SR 951.11

obligations.title: Add the duty: Deliver statistical data on the business to the Swiss National Bank
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, NBG (SR 951.11), Art. 15 Abs. 1 und 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Deliver statistical data on the business to the Swiss National Bank

summaries.en: Banks, financial market infrastructures, the financial institutions under the Financial Institutions Act and the licence holders under Article 13 paragraph 2 of the Collective Investment Schemes Act must supply the Swiss National Bank with statistical data on their activity. The National Bank lays down in an ordinance which data are to be delivered and at what intervals.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hold minimum reserves at the rate the National Bank sets
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, NBG (SR 951.11), Art. 17 Abs. 1, Art. 18 Abs. 1 und 2, Art. 23 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Hold minimum reserves at the rate the National Bank sets

summaries.en: Banks must maintain minimum reserves, held as Swiss franc coins, banknotes and sight deposits at the National Bank, at the rate the National Bank sets for the average of a given period. The rate may not exceed 4 per cent of the banks' short-term liabilities in Swiss francs, which are liabilities at sight or with a remaining term of up to three months and liabilities from callable customer deposits other than tied pension funds. A bank that falls short pays the National Bank interest on the shortfall for as long as it lasts.

payload.refLabel: Art. 17 Abs. 1, Art. 18 Abs. 1 und 2, Art. 23 Abs. 1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Prove regularly to the National Bank that the minimum reserves are held
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, NBG (SR 951.11), Art. 18 Abs. 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Prove regularly to the National Bank that the minimum reserves are held

summaries.en: Banks must regularly provide the Swiss National Bank with proof that they hold minimum reserves in the amount required.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the National Bank the information it needs to oversee financial market infrastructures
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, NBG (SR 951.11), Art. 20 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2023

titles.en: Give the National Bank the information it needs to oversee financial market infrastructures

summaries.en: Central counterparties, central securities depositories, payment systems and DLT trading facilities must give the Swiss National Bank, on request, all information and documents it needs to detect risks to the stability of the financial system early and to judge systemic importance. Systemically important financial market infrastructures and their audit firms must give it all information and documents it needs for its tasks and must report to it without delay events of material importance for its oversight.

instruments.title: Add FINMAG, the Swiss Financial Market Supervision Act (Finanzmarktaufsichtsgesetz), for its duties on supervised firms
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht (Finanzmarktaufsichtsgesetz, FINMAG), SR 956.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. April 2025, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 61 ("Übrige Bestimmungen: 1. Januar 2009"; the organisational provisions it lists on 1. Februar 2008)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über die Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht (Finanzmarktaufsichtsgesetz, FINMAG)
titles.en: Financial Market Supervision Act (Federal Act on the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority)

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 22. Juni 2007 über die Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht (Finanzmarktaufsichtsgesetz, FINMAG), SR 956.1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give FINMA all the information and documents it needs
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMAG (SR 956.1), Art. 29 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Give FINMA all the information and documents it needs

summaries.en: Supervised persons and entities, their audit firms and auditors, and persons and companies that hold a qualified or controlling participation in them must give FINMA all information and hand over all documents it needs to carry out its tasks.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report events of material importance for supervision to FINMA without delay
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMAG (SR 956.1), Art. 29 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Report events of material importance for supervision to FINMA without delay

summaries.en: Supervised persons and entities, and the audit firms that audit them, must report to FINMA without delay any event that is of material importance for supervision.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the audit firm all it needs and tell FINMA which audit firm was chosen
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMAG (SR 956.1), Art. 25, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Give the audit firm all it needs and tell FINMA which audit firm was chosen

summaries.en: Where an audit firm is appointed for the audit or FINMA calls in an audit agent, the supervised firm must give them all information and hand over all documents they need to carry out their tasks. The supervised firm must inform FINMA of its choice of audit firm.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pass non-public information to foreign authorities only under the act's conditions
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMAG (SR 956.1), Art. 42c Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Pass non-public information to foreign authorities only under the act's conditions

summaries.en: A supervised firm may transmit non-public information to the competent foreign financial market supervisors and other foreign bodies entrusted with supervision only if the information is used solely to enforce financial market law, the recipients are bound by official or professional secrecy, and the rights of clients and third parties are preserved. It may also transmit non-public information on transactions of clients and supervised firms to foreign authorities and the bodies they mandate if those rights are preserved. A transmission of material importance must be reported to FINMA beforehand.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give foreign supervisors and FINMA the information needed for cross-border audits
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FINMAG (SR 956.1), Art. 43 Abs. 5 und 6, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. April 2025

titles.en: Give foreign supervisors and FINMA the information needed for cross-border audits

summaries.en: Establishments organised under Swiss law, which are the subsidiaries, branches and representative offices of supervised firms or foreign institutions and other undertakings included in consolidated supervision, must give the competent foreign financial market supervisors and FINMA the information needed for direct audits or for administrative assistance by FINMA, and must let them inspect their books.

instruments.title: Add VAG, the Swiss Insurance Supervision Act (Versicherungsaufsichtsgesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz betreffend die Aufsicht über Versicherungsunternehmen (Versicherungsaufsichtsgesetz, VAG), SR 961.01, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. September 2024, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 91: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. Januar 2006" (footnote: BRB vom 9. Nov. 2005)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz betreffend die Aufsicht über Versicherungsunternehmen (Versicherungsaufsichtsgesetz, VAG)
titles.en: Insurance Supervision Act (Federal Act on the Supervision of Insurance Companies)

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 17. Dezember 2004 betreffend die Aufsicht über Versicherungsunternehmen (Versicherungsaufsichtsgesetz, VAG), SR 961.01

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep sufficient solvency as an insurer
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 9, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Keep sufficient solvency as an insurer

summaries.en: An insurance company must have sufficient solvency. Solvency is sufficient when the risk-bearing capital is at least as large as the target capital.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Set up sufficient technical provisions and secure claims with tied assets
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 16 Abs. 1 und Art. 17, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Set up sufficient technical provisions and secure claims with tied assets

summaries.en: An insurance company must set up sufficient technical provisions for its whole business and must secure the claims arising from insurance contracts with tied assets. No tied assets may be formed for the insurance portfolios of foreign branches of insurers based in Switzerland, and the tied assets may not be used to secure those portfolios.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Organise the insurer to control all material risks, with an internal control system and an internal audit
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 22 Abs. 1 und Art. 27, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Organise the insurer to control all material risks, with an internal control system and an internal audit

summaries.en: An insurance company must be organised so that it can in particular identify, limit and monitor all material risks. It sets up an effective internal control system covering its whole business and appoints an internal audit function that is independent of management.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Appoint a responsible actuary and report the actuary's departure to FINMA at once
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 23 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Appoint a responsible actuary and report the actuary's departure to FINMA at once

summaries.en: An insurance company must appoint a responsible actuary and give that person access to all business records. The actuary must be of good repute, professionally qualified and able to assess correctly the financial consequences of the company's activity. The company must notify FINMA without delay when the responsible actuary is dismissed or resigns.

obligations.title: Add the duty: File the annual report and the supervisory report with FINMA by 30 April
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 25 Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: File the annual report and the supervisory report with FINMA by 30 April

summaries.en: An insurance company draws up each year as at 31 December an annual report made up of the annual accounts, the management report and, where the law requires or the company belongs to an insurance group or conglomerate, consolidated accounts, and also a supervisory report whose requirements FINMA sets. It files both for the past financial year with FINMA by the following 30 April. A foreign insurer files a separate annual report and supervisory report for its business in Switzerland.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Draw up a key information document for qualified life insurance and hand it over before the contract
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 39b Abs. 1 und Art. 39h, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Draw up a key information document for qualified life insurance and hand it over before the contract

summaries.en: An insurance company that offers a qualified life insurance must first draw up a key information document for it. When recommending such an insurance, insurers and insurance intermediaries give the policyholder that document free of charge before the contract is concluded. The insurer also informs the policyholder of third-party compensation it has accepted in connection with qualified life insurance.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Check that a qualified life insurance is appropriate before recommending it
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 39j, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Check that a qualified life insurance is appropriate before recommending it

summaries.en: Before recommending a qualified life insurance, the insurer or insurance intermediary must ask about the policyholder's knowledge and experience and check whether the insurance is appropriate for that person. If it is not appropriate, they advise against the contract; if the information received is not enough to judge, they tell the policyholder that no assessment is made. No check is needed where the contract is concluded at the policyholder's own initiative without personal advice.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register with FINMA before acting as an untied insurance intermediary
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 41 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Register with FINMA before acting as an untied insurance intermediary

summaries.en: Untied insurance intermediaries may act only if they are entered in FINMA's register. They are entered if they prove that they have their seat, residence or a branch in Switzerland, are of good repute and assure compliance with the act, have the necessary skills and knowledge or, as employers, enough employees who do, and have professional liability insurance or equivalent financial security.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell policyholders who the intermediary is, whether it is tied and who is liable
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 45, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Tell policyholders who the intermediary is, whether it is tied and who is liable

summaries.en: An insurance intermediary must tell policyholders its name and address, whether it acts as a tied or untied intermediary and, if tied, the name and address of the insurers it acts for, how they can find out about its training, who can be held liable for negligence, errors or incorrect information in the intermediation, and how personal data are processed. The information must be understandable and may be given in standardised form on paper or electronically. It must be handed over so that policyholders can know it when they apply for or accept the insurance contract.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Prevent conflicts of interest in insurance intermediation or disclose them before the contract
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 45a Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Prevent conflicts of interest in insurance intermediation or disclose them before the contract

summaries.en: An insurance intermediary must take appropriate organisational measures to avoid conflicts of interest that can arise in the intermediation of insurance services, or to rule out that policyholders are disadvantaged by them. Where a disadvantage cannot be ruled out, this must be disclosed to the policyholders before the insurance contract is concluded.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Disclose compensation from insurers to policyholders as an untied intermediary
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VAG (SR 961.01), Art. 45b Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. September 2024

titles.en: Disclose compensation from insurers to policyholders as an untied intermediary

summaries.en: An untied insurance intermediary may accept compensation from insurers or other third parties only if it has expressly informed the policyholders about it. If it is also paid by the policyholder, it may accept such compensation only if the policyholder, expressly informed, expressly waives having it passed on, or if it passes the compensation on in full. The information states the type and amount before the service is provided or the contract concluded, or the calculation parameters and ranges where the amount cannot be known in advance, and the amounts actually received are disclosed on request.

instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über den Versicherungsvertrag (Versicherungsvertragsgesetz, VVG), SR 221.229.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Januar 2024, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 104: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. Januar 1910" (footnote: BRB vom 17. Juli 1908, AS 24 756)

titles.en: Insurance Contract Act
