obligations.title: Add the duty: Inform the policyholder about the insurer and the main content of the contract before it is concluded
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VVG (SR 221.229.1), Art. 3 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2024

titles.en: Inform the policyholder about the insurer and the main content of the contract before it is concluded

summaries.en: Before the insurance contract is concluded, the insurer must inform the policyholder, understandably and in a form that can be evidenced by text, about its identity and the main content of the contract: the risks insured, the scope of cover, the premiums and other duties, the term and ending of the contract, surplus participation, surrender values, the processing of personal data, the right of withdrawal and the time limit for reporting a claim, among other points. The information must be handed over so that the policyholder can know it when applying for or accepting the contract, and by then the policyholder must hold the general insurance conditions and the data processing information.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Accept the policyholder's withdrawal within 14 days
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VVG (SR 221.229.1), Art. 2a Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2024

titles.en: Accept the policyholder's withdrawal within 14 days

summaries.en: The policyholder may withdraw the application to conclude the contract or the acceptance of it, in writing or in another form that can be evidenced by text, within 14 days from applying for or accepting the contract. The period is met if the withdrawal is communicated to the insurer or posted on its last day. There is no right of withdrawal for collective personal insurance, provisional cover and agreements with a term of less than one month.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Issue a policy and, on request, a copy of the applicant's declarations
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VVG (SR 221.229.1), Art. 11, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2024

titles.en: Issue a policy and, on request, a copy of the applicant's declarations

summaries.en: The insurer issues the policyholder a policy that records the rights and duties of the parties. On request it must give the policyholder a copy of the declarations, made in the application or otherwise, on the basis of which the insurance was concluded.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Pay claims four weeks after receiving the details that establish them
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, VVG (SR 221.229.1), Art. 41 und Art. 41a Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2024

titles.en: Pay claims four weeks after receiving the details that establish them

summaries.en: A claim under the insurance contract falls due four weeks after the insurer has received the details from which it can satisfy itself that the claim is justified; a clause that makes the claim due only on the insurer's acknowledgement or a final judgment is invalid. Where the insurer disputes its liability, the entitled person may after that period demand payments on account up to the undisputed amount.

instruments.title: Add GwG, the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (Geldwäschereigesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Bekämpfung der Geldwäscherei und der Terrorismusfinanzierung (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG), SR 955.0, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Oktober 2026, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 44: "Datum des Inkrafttretens: 1. April 1998" (footnote: BRB vom 16. März 1998)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über die Bekämpfung der Geldwäscherei und der Terrorismusfinanzierung (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG)
titles.en: Anti-Money Laundering Act (Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing)

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 10. Oktober 1997 über die Bekämpfung der Geldwäscherei und der Terrorismusfinanzierung (Geldwäschereigesetz, GwG), SR 955.0

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify the contracting party when a business relationship begins
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 3 Abs. 1, 2 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Identify the contracting party when a business relationship begins

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must identify the contracting party on the basis of a conclusive document when it enters into a business relationship; for a legal entity it must take note of its provisions on powers of representation and verify the identity of the persons who open the relationship in its name. For cash transactions with a party not yet identified, the duty applies only when one transaction or several that appear connected reach a significant value, and always when there are grounds to suspect money laundering or terrorist financing.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Establish the beneficial owner and verify that person's identity
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Establish the beneficial owner and verify that person's identity

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must establish the beneficial owner with the care the circumstances require and verify that person's identity; it may do without this where the contracting party is a listed company or a subsidiary majority-controlled by one. It must obtain a written or otherwise text-evidenced declaration of who the beneficial owner is where the contracting party is not the beneficial owner or there is doubt, where the party is a domiciliary company or an operating legal entity, or where a cash transaction of significant value is carried out. From parties holding collective accounts or deposits it must require a full list of the beneficial owners and immediate notice of every change.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Repeat the identification when doubts arise during the relationship
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 5 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Repeat the identification when doubts arise during the relationship

summaries.en: If doubts arise in the course of the business relationship about the identity of the contracting party or about the beneficial ownership, the financial intermediary must repeat the identification or the establishment of the beneficial owner.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Establish the nature and purpose of the business relationship on a risk basis
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 6 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Establish the nature and purpose of the business relationship on a risk basis

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must identify the nature and purpose of the business relationship the contracting party wants. The extent of the information to obtain, the level of hierarchy at which the decision to enter into or continue the relationship is taken, and the frequency of checks depend on the risk the contracting party represents.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Clarify the background of unusual and high-risk transactions and relationships
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 6 Abs. 2 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Clarify the background of unusual and high-risk transactions and relationships

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must clarify the background and purpose of a transaction or business relationship that appears unusual, unless it is plainly lawful, that carries a higher risk, for which there are indications that assets stem from a crime or a qualified tax offence, are controlled by a criminal or terrorist organisation or serve terrorist financing, or where the data match or closely resemble data forwarded to it under Article 22a. Relationships with foreign politically exposed persons and those close to them always count as higher risk; those with domestic politically exposed persons and those of international organisations count as higher risk together with one or more further risk criteria.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Document transactions and clarifications and keep the records for at least ten years
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Document transactions and clarifications and keep the records for at least ten years

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must keep records of the transactions carried out and of the clarifications the act requires in such a way that expert third parties can form a reliable judgement on the transactions and relationships and on compliance with the act. It checks the records periodically for being up to date and updates them as needed, at intervals and to an extent that depend on the customer's risk. It keeps them so that it can answer requests from prosecution authorities within a reasonable time, and for at least ten years after the relationship ends or the transaction is completed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Take organisational measures against money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions breaches
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 8, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Take organisational measures against money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions breaches

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must take the organisational measures needed in its field to prevent money laundering and terrorist financing and breaches of coercive measures under the Embargo Act. In particular it must ensure that staff are sufficiently trained and that controls are carried out.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report suspicions of money laundering or terrorist financing to the reporting office at once
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 9 Abs. 1, 1quater und 1quinquies, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Report suspicions of money laundering or terrorist financing to the reporting office at once

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must report to the Money Laundering Reporting Office without delay when it knows or has reasonable grounds to suspect that assets involved in the business relationship are connected with money laundering under Article 305bis or an offence under Article 260ter of the Criminal Code, stem from a crime or a qualified tax offence, are subject to the power of disposal of a criminal or terrorist organisation or serve terrorist financing, when it breaks off negotiations because of such a suspicion, or when its clarifications show a match with data forwarded under Article 22a. A suspicion is reasonable when there is a concrete indication or several clues that cannot be dispelled by further clarification under Article 6. The report must name the intermediary; the staff handling the case may be anonymised if they can still be reached at once.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a paper trail for reported assets and tell the reporting office when the relationship ends
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 9a und 9b, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Keep a paper trail for reported assets and tell the reporting office when the relationship ends

summaries.en: While the reporting office analyses a report, the financial intermediary carries out customer orders concerning the reported assets, and orders concerning significant assets only in a form that lets prosecution authorities follow their trail. If the office does not tell it within 40 working days that the report has been passed to a prosecution authority, the intermediary may end the relationship, but may allow significant assets to be withdrawn only in such a traceable form. It must tell the reporting office without delay that the relationship has ended and on what date.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Freeze reported assets when the reporting office forwards the case
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 10, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Freeze reported assets when the reporting office forwards the case

summaries.en: A financial intermediary must freeze the assets entrusted to it that are connected with a report as soon as the reporting office tells it that the report has been passed to a prosecution authority, and must freeze at once assets connected with a report made because of a match with data forwarded under Article 22a. It maintains the freeze until an order from the competent prosecution authority arrives, but for no more than five working days from the office's notice or, in the second case, from its own report.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Do not tell the persons concerned or third parties that a report was made
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 10a Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Do not tell the persons concerned or third parties that a report was made

summaries.en: A financial intermediary may not inform the persons concerned or third parties that it has made a report; the authorities and organisations responsible for supervision and the persons who audit for them do not count as third parties. Where this is needed to meet the act's duties, it may inform another intermediary subject to the act that is able to freeze the assets, one with which it jointly serves a client's asset management under a contractual cooperation, or one of the same group, and it may inform its foreign parent company if that company undertakes to keep the ban. An intermediary informed in this way is bound by the same ban.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Hand over further information to the reporting office on request
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, GwG (SR 955.0), Art. 11a Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Hand over further information to the reporting office on request

summaries.en: A financial intermediary that has made a report must hand over to the Money Laundering Reporting Office, on request, the further information the office needs for its analysis, as far as the intermediary holds it. Other financial intermediaries that the analysis, or information from a foreign reporting office, shows to be or to have been involved in the relationship or transaction must likewise hand over all related information they hold. The office sets the time limit for handing it over.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify the company's own beneficial owners, verify them and keep the records for ten years
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, TJPG (SR 955.3), Art. 7 Abs. 1 und 2, Art. 8 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Identify the company's own beneficial owners, verify them and keep the records for ten years

summaries.en: A company subject to the act must identify its beneficial owners, obtaining their name, date of birth, nationality, address and state of residence and the necessary information on the nature and extent of the control they exercise, and must verify their identity and status with the care the circumstances require. It documents this information, keeps it up to date and ensures it can be accessed in Switzerland at any time; where it could not identify or satisfactorily verify a beneficial owner, it documents that fact and the steps taken. It keeps the information and supporting documents for ten years after the person has ceased to be a beneficial owner.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report the company's beneficial owners and every change to the transparency register within a month
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, TJPG (SR 955.3), Art. 9 Abs. 1, 3 und 4, Art. 10 und Art. 51, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2026

titles.en: Report the company's beneficial owners and every change to the transparency register within a month

summaries.en: A company subject to the act must report the identity of its beneficial owners to the transparency register within one month of its entry in the commercial register, or of becoming subject to the act in the case of a foreign legal entity, stating so if it could not identify or verify a beneficial owner. It must report every change to a fact entered in the register within one month of learning of it. For Swiss legal entities that existed when the act entered into force, a transitional provision requires the first report within one month of the next change to their commercial register entry and at the latest within three to six months of the entry into force, depending on their legal form and audit duty, or within two years where all beneficial owners are already entered in the commercial register as members or officers.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Comply with the coercive measures the Federal Council enacts as sanctions ordinances
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, EmbG (SR 946.231), Art. 1 Abs. 3, Art. 2 Abs. 3 und Art. 9, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Juli 2023

titles.en: Comply with the coercive measures the Federal Council enacts as sanctions ordinances

summaries.en: Coercive measures to enforce international sanctions are enacted by the Federal Council as ordinances; they may restrict trade in goods and services, payments, capital movements and the movement of persons, and may include bans and licensing and reporting duties. Anyone who intentionally breaches a provision of such an ordinance whose breach is declared punishable is liable to a custodial sentence of up to one year or a monetary penalty, and of up to five years in serious cases. A negligent breach carries a fine of up to 100,000 francs.

obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, EmbG (SR 946.231), Art. 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Juli 2023

titles.en: Give the sanctions control bodies the information and documents they need

summaries.en: Anyone who is directly or indirectly affected by measures under the act must give the control bodies the Federal Council designates the information, and submit the documents, that are needed for a full assessment or control.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report assets caught by a freezing order to the Money Laundering Reporting Office at once
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, SRVG (SR 196.1), Art. 7 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Juli 2016

titles.en: Report assets caught by a freezing order to the Money Laundering Reporting Office at once

summaries.en: Persons and institutions that hold or manage in Switzerland assets of persons who fall under a freezing measure ordered with a view to mutual legal assistance must report those assets to the Money Laundering Reporting Office without delay. The same duty binds persons and institutions that do not hold or manage such assets but know of them because of their tasks. Lawyers and notaries are exempt as far as their activity is covered by professional secrecy.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Give the reporting office the information and documents it asks for on frozen assets
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, SRVG (SR 196.1), Art. 7 Abs. 3 und 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Juli 2016

titles.en: Give the reporting office the information and documents it asks for on frozen assets

summaries.en: The Money Laundering Reporting Office may ask any person or institution that might hold or manage assets frozen under the act for information about them. Those who have reported or been asked must also, on request, give the office all information and submit all documents on the reported assets that are needed to implement the act, as far as they hold them.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Go on managing frozen assets and warn the foreign ministry of a rapid loss in value
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, SRVG (SR 196.1), Art. 8 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Juli 2016

titles.en: Go on managing frozen assets and warn the foreign ministry of a rapid loss in value

summaries.en: Persons and institutions that hold or manage in Switzerland assets of persons who fall under a freezing measure continue to manage the assets after the freeze. They must inform the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs without delay if a rapid loss in value threatens or the assets are costly to maintain, and must give it on request all information and documents on the freeze and the management of the assets.

instruments.title: Add DSG, the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (Datenschutzgesetz)
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über den Datenschutz (Datenschutzgesetz, DSG), SR 235.1, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 7. Juli 2025, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 74: "Inkrafttreten: 1. September 2023" (footnote: BRB vom 31. Aug. 2022)

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über den Datenschutz (Datenschutzgesetz, DSG)
titles.en: Federal Act on Data Protection

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 25. September 2020 über den Datenschutz (Datenschutzgesetz, DSG), SR 235.1

obligations.title: Add the duty: Process personal data lawfully, in good faith, proportionately and for a recognisable purpose
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 6 Abs. 1 bis 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Process personal data lawfully, in good faith, proportionately and for a recognisable purpose

summaries.en: Personal data must be processed lawfully, in good faith and proportionately, may be collected only for a specific purpose the data subject can recognise and may be processed only in a way compatible with that purpose. They are destroyed or anonymised as soon as they are no longer needed for the purpose. Whoever processes personal data must make sure they are accurate and take all appropriate measures so that data that are incorrect or incomplete for their purpose are corrected, deleted or destroyed.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Build data protection into systems by design and by default
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Build data protection into systems by design and by default

summaries.en: The controller must set up the data processing, technically and organisationally and from the planning stage, so that the data protection rules and in particular the processing principles are complied with. The measures must be appropriate to the state of the art, the type and extent of the processing and the risk to the personality or fundamental rights of the data subjects. Suitable default settings must ensure that processing is limited to the minimum the purpose needs, unless the data subject decides otherwise.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Ensure data security appropriate to the risk
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 8 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Ensure data security appropriate to the risk

summaries.en: The controller and the processor must ensure, through suitable technical and organisational measures, a level of data security appropriate to the risk. The measures must make it possible to avoid breaches of data security.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Entrust processing to a processor only under the act's conditions and check its data security
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 9 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Entrust processing to a processor only under the act's conditions and check its data security

summaries.en: Processing of personal data may be entrusted to a processor by contract or by legislation only if the data are processed as the controller itself would be allowed to and no statutory or contractual duty of confidentiality forbids it. The controller must satisfy itself in particular that the processor is able to ensure data security. The processor may pass the processing on to a third party only with the controller's prior approval.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep a register of processing activities
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 12 Abs. 1, 2, 3 und 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Keep a register of processing activities

summaries.en: Controllers and processors must each keep a register of their processing activities. The controller's register contains at least its identity, the purpose of processing, the categories of data subjects, of personal data and of recipients, where possible the retention period and a general description of the security measures, and for disclosures abroad the state and the safeguards. The Federal Council provides exceptions for companies with fewer than 250 employees whose processing carries a low risk.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Disclose personal data abroad only where adequate protection is ensured
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 16 Abs. 1 und 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Disclose personal data abroad only where adequate protection is ensured

summaries.en: Personal data may be disclosed abroad if the Federal Council has determined that the legislation of the state concerned or the international body ensures adequate protection. Without such a decision they may be disclosed only if suitable protection is ensured by an international treaty, by contractual data protection clauses notified to the federal commissioner beforehand, by standard data protection clauses the commissioner has approved, issued or recognised, or by binding corporate rules approved beforehand by the commissioner or by the data protection authority of a state with adequate protection.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Inform data subjects when their personal data are collected
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 19, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Inform data subjects when their personal data are collected

summaries.en: The controller must inform the data subject appropriately about the collection of personal data, also where the data are not collected from that person, giving at least its identity and contact details, the purpose of processing and any recipients or categories of recipients. Where data are not collected from the data subject it also states the categories of data, and where data go abroad the state or international body and any safeguards. For data not collected from the data subject the information is given within one month of receiving the data, or at the latest on disclosure if the data are disclosed earlier.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell the person concerned about an automated individual decision and offer a human review
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 21 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Tell the person concerned about an automated individual decision and offer a human review

summaries.en: The controller must inform the data subject of a decision that rests solely on automated processing and has a legal consequence for that person or affects them considerably. On request it lets the person state their view, and the person can demand that the decision be reviewed by a natural person. This does not apply where the decision is directly connected with concluding or performing a contract with the person and their request is granted, or where the person has expressly consented to an automated decision.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Carry out a data protection impact assessment before high-risk processing
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 22 Abs. 1 bis 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Carry out a data protection impact assessment before high-risk processing

summaries.en: The controller must draw up a data protection impact assessment beforehand when processing may entail a high risk to the personality or fundamental rights of the data subject, as in particular with the extensive processing of sensitive personal data or the systematic monitoring of extensive public areas. The assessment describes the planned processing, evaluates the risks and sets out the protective measures. Private controllers are exempt where they are obliged by law to process the data, and may do without it where they use a certified system, product or service or keep to a code of conduct that meets the act's conditions.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report high-risk data security breaches to the federal commissioner as quickly as possible
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 24 Abs. 1 bis 5, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Report high-risk data security breaches to the federal commissioner as quickly as possible

summaries.en: The controller must report to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner as quickly as possible a breach of data security that is likely to lead to a high risk to the personality or fundamental rights of the data subject, stating at least the nature of the breach, its consequences and the measures taken or planned. A processor reports a breach to the controller as quickly as possible. The controller informs the data subject where this is needed for their protection or the commissioner requires it, subject to the limits the article allows.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Answer a data subject's access request free of charge, as a rule within 30 days
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, DSG (SR 235.1), Art. 25 Abs. 1, 2, 6 und 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 7. Juli 2025

titles.en: Answer a data subject's access request free of charge, as a rule within 30 days

summaries.en: Any person may ask the controller whether personal data about them are being processed. The person receives the information needed to assert their rights and to ensure transparent processing, in every case the controller's identity and contact details, the data processed, the purpose, the retention period or the criteria for it, the available information on the origin of the data, whether an automated individual decision exists and its logic, and any recipients. The controller must provide the information free of charge and as a rule within 30 days.

instruments.title: Add ISG, the Swiss Information Security Act (Informationssicherheitsgesetz), for its duty to report cyberattacks
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Informationssicherheit (Informationssicherheitsgesetz, ISG), SR 128, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 1. Oktober 2025, the version in force on 14 November 2026; entry into force read in Art. 92 ("Die übrigen Bestimmungen: 1. Januar 2024"; Art. 87 on 1. Mai 2022); the cyberattack reporting section is "in Kraft seit 1. April 2025" by the footnote to its heading

titles.de: Bundesgesetz über die Informationssicherheit (Informationssicherheitsgesetz, ISG)
titles.en: Information Security Act (Federal Act on Information Security)

payload.officialRef: Bundesgesetz vom 18. Dezember 2020 über die Informationssicherheit (Informationssicherheitsgesetz, ISG), SR 128

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report serious cyberattacks on the firm's information systems to the Federal Office for Cybersecurity
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ISG (SR 128), Art. 74a Abs. 1, Art. 74b Abs. 1 Bst. e und Art. 74d, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2025

titles.en: Report serious cyberattacks on the firm's information systems to the Federal Office for Cybersecurity

summaries.en: Companies subject to the Banking Act, the Insurance Supervision Act or the Financial Market Infrastructure Act are among the organisations that must ensure that cyberattacks on their information systems are reported to the Federal Office for Cybersecurity. An attack must be reported if it endangers the functioning of the critical infrastructure concerned, has led to manipulation or leakage of information, remained undetected for a long period, in particular where there are signs that it prepared further attacks, or involves extortion, threats or coercion. The duty covers attacks with effects in Switzerland even where the systems are abroad, and not attacks that affect only activities outside the listed ones.

payload.refLabel: Art. 74a Abs. 1, Art. 74b Abs. 1 Bst. e und Art. 74d

obligations.title: Add the duty: Make the cyberattack report within 24 hours of discovery and complete it as facts emerge
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, ISG (SR 128), Art. 74e Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Oktober 2025

titles.en: Make the cyberattack report within 24 hours of discovery and complete it as facts emerge

summaries.en: The report must be made within 24 hours of the cyberattack being discovered. It must contain information on the reporting organisation, the type and execution of the attack, its effects, the measures taken and, as far as known, the further steps planned. If not all the required information is known when the report is made, the organisation supplements it as soon as it has new information.

titles.en: Federal Act on the International Automatic Exchange of Information in Tax Matters

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register with the Federal Tax Administration as a reporting Swiss financial institution
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAG (SR 653.1), Art. 13 Abs. 1 bis 3, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Register with the Federal Tax Administration as a reporting Swiss financial institution

summaries.en: Whoever becomes a reporting Swiss financial institution under an applicable agreement and the act must register with the Federal Tax Administration without being asked, stating its name and seat, its business identification number, the type of activity and the date it began. It must deregister, again without being asked, when it ceases to be a reporting institution or gives up its business.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report account information to the Federal Tax Administration within six months of the year end
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAG (SR 653.1), Art. 15 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Report account information to the Federal Tax Administration within six months of the year end

summaries.en: A reporting Swiss financial institution must transmit electronically to the Federal Tax Administration, each year within six months of the end of the calendar year concerned, the information to be transmitted under the applicable agreement and the information on its undocumented accounts. If it maintains no reportable accounts, it reports that fact within the same period.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Tell reportable persons by 31 January that their account data will be exchanged
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAG (SR 653.1), Art. 14, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Tell reportable persons by 31 January that their account data will be exchanged

summaries.en: A reporting Swiss financial institution must inform reportable persons, directly or through its contracting party, at the latest on 31 January of the year in which information about them is first transmitted to a partner state, about its status as a reporting institution, the agreements and the information exchanged under them, the list of partner states, the permitted use of the information and their rights under data protection law and this act. It publishes on its website a list of partner states updated each year on 31 January or refers to the finance department's list. On request it gives the account holder a copy of the report.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Obtain the self-certification at account opening and close or block the account if it is missing after 90 days
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAG (SR 653.1), Art. 11 Abs. 7 bis 9, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Obtain the self-certification at account opening and close or block the account if it is missing after 90 days

summaries.en: A reporting Swiss financial institution must take appropriate organisational measures to ensure that it holds all the information to be collected at account opening, in particular the self-certification. It may open a new account without one only where the holder is an entity it can reasonably determine to be non-reportable, or in another exceptional case, where it must receive and check the self-certification within 90 days. If 90 days after opening it lacks the information needed to check the self-certification, or in an exceptional case the self-certification itself, it must close the account or block all inflows and outflows until it has everything, subject to the cases under Article 9 of the Anti-Money Laundering Act.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Keep the due diligence documents under the accounting retention rules
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAG (SR 653.1), Art. 17a, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Keep the due diligence documents under the accounting retention rules

summaries.en: Reporting Swiss financial institutions and relevant reporting crypto-asset service providers must keep the documents drawn up and the evidence obtained to meet their duties under the agreements and the act in accordance with Article 958f of the Code of Obligations.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register as a reporting crypto-asset service provider and report transactions each year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAG (SR 653.1), Art. 13a Abs. 1 bis 3 und Art. 15 Abs. 1bis, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Register as a reporting crypto-asset service provider and report transactions each year

summaries.en: Whoever becomes a relevant reporting crypto-asset service provider under an applicable agreement and the act must register with the Federal Tax Administration without being asked and deregister when that status ends or the business is given up. A Swiss reporting crypto-asset service provider transmits electronically to the Federal Tax Administration, each year within six months of the end of the calendar year, the information to be transmitted under the applicable agreement, or reports within the same period that it carried out no reportable transactions.

payload.refLabel: Art. 13a Abs. 1 bis 3 und Art. 15 Abs. 1bis

obligations.title: Add the duty: Obtain a self-certification from crypto-asset users and stop transactions if it is missing
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, AIAG (SR 653.1), Art. 12f Abs. 1 bis 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 1. Januar 2026

titles.en: Obtain a self-certification from crypto-asset users and stop transactions if it is missing

summaries.en: A Swiss reporting crypto-asset service provider must take appropriate organisational measures to ensure that it holds the self-certification when it begins a business relationship with a crypto-asset user, and for existing users within 12 months of the entry into force of the amendment of 26 September 2025. It may begin a relationship without one where the user is an entity it can reasonably determine to be an excluded person, or in another exceptional case, where it must receive and check the self-certification within 90 days. If the information needed is missing 90 days after the relationship began, or after the 12 months for existing users, it must end the relationship or carry out no relevant transactions for the user until it has everything.

instruments.title: Add the FATCA-Gesetz, the Swiss act implementing the FATCA agreement with the United States
instruments.sourceLabel: Fedlex, Bundesgesetz über die Umsetzung des FATCA-Abkommens zwischen der Schweiz und den Vereinigten Staaten (FATCA-Gesetz), SR 672.933.6, consolidated German text (file store), Stand am 30. titles.en: FATCA Act (Federal Act on the Implementation of the FATCA Agreement between Switzerland and the United States)

obligations.title: Add the duty: Register with the United States Internal Revenue Service
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FATCA-Gesetz (SR 672.933.6), Art. 4, consolidated German text, Stand am 30. Juni 2014

titles.en: Register with the United States Internal Revenue Service

summaries.en: Swiss financial institutions must register with the United States Internal Revenue Service. Institutions listed in the relevant parts of Annex II of the FATCA agreement, and those that United States law treats as exempt beneficial owners or as deemed-compliant institutions without a registration duty, are exempt.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Meet the obligations of the agreement with the IRS for the whole customer base
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FATCA-Gesetz (SR 672.933.6), Art. 5 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 30. Juni 2014

titles.en: Meet the obligations of the agreement with the IRS for the whole customer base

summaries.en: Swiss financial institutions registered with the United States Internal Revenue Service must fulfil the obligations arising from the agreement with it that the FATCA agreement provides for, in respect of their entire customer base.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Identify the US accounts the institution maintains
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FATCA-Gesetz (SR 672.933.6), Art. 7, consolidated German text, Stand am 30. Juni 2014

titles.en: Identify the US accounts the institution maintains

summaries.en: Reporting Swiss financial institutions must identify the US accounts they maintain in accordance with Annex I of the FATCA agreement.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Open a new US account only with the holder's consent to reporting and close it if no US tax number arrives
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FATCA-Gesetz (SR 672.933.6), Art. 9, consolidated German text, Stand am 30. Juni 2014

titles.en: Open a new US account only with the holder's consent to reporting and close it if no US tax number arrives

summaries.en: A reporting Swiss financial institution may open a new US account only if the account holder consents to the account data being reported to the United States Internal Revenue Service, and must close the account if the holder does not supply the US taxpayer identification number within 90 days of opening. Where it expects to pay a foreign reportable amount in connection with a new account for, or an obligation towards, a non-participating financial institution, it must obtain that institution's consent to reporting before opening the account or entering into the obligation.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Report US accounts to the IRS every year
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FATCA-Gesetz (SR 672.933.6), Art. 10 Abs. 1, consolidated German text, Stand am 30. Juni 2014

titles.en: Report US accounts to the IRS every year

summaries.en: A reporting Swiss financial institution reports to the United States Internal Revenue Service each year, for US accounts, the account data of the US persons who have consented, under the applicable United States Treasury regulations. By 31 January of the following year it reports the number and total assets of all US accounts for which the holder has not consented.

obligations.title: Add the duty: Deliver account data to the Federal Tax Administration within 10 days of a group request
obligations.sourceLabel: Fedlex, FATCA-Gesetz (SR 672.933.6), Art. 12 Abs. 2, consolidated German text, Stand am 30. Juni 2014

titles.en: Deliver account data to the Federal Tax Administration within 10 days of a group request

summaries.en: When a group request from the United States arrives, the Federal Tax Administration asks the reporting Swiss financial institution to send it separately, within 10 days, the reportable data in electronic form and the documents that let it check whether an account is reportable.
